tools.name: validate_program
tools.description: Check a Rhylthyme program for structural and scheduling errors BEFORE visualizing or saving it: missing/duplicate ids, dangling afterStep references, dependency cycles, steps that overlap within a track, tasks with no resourceConstraint, unparseable durations, invalid choice references, and schema 0

tools.name: analyze_schedule

tools.name: visualize_schedule
tools.description: Render a multi-step parallel schedule as a live timeline (cooking, lab protocols, event run-of-show, training). **Call this for ANY schedule you produce — imported, catalog match, or built freehand.** A schedule belongs in a visualization, never in prose. The program is validated first (same checks

tools.name: import_from_source
tools.description: Import a recipe or lab protocol from an external source into a Rhylthyme program. Sources: spoonacular (recipes, preferred), themealdb (recipes, fallback), protocolsio (lab protocols), cooklang (.cook recipe URL — action must be 'import', query is the URL; GitHub blob URLs are auto-converted), opent

tools.name: import_text
tools.description: Turn a block of pasted text — a recipe, a lab protocol, a run-of-show, a training plan — into a validated multi-track Rhylthyme program. Use when the user pastes the steps themselves and no structural importer fits (no URL, no supported service, a photo they transcribed, a PDF they copied out of). R

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Create a Rhylthyme environment definition with resource constraints for a workspace (lab, kitchen, bakery, etc.). Returns environment JSON; copy its resourceConstraints into the program (or reference it by environmentId) before calling **visualize_schedule**.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Sign in to your Rhylthyme account so you can list and save your schedules and import from external sources. Opens a browser page where you log in (Google, Apple, or email). After signing in, copy the token displayed on the page and provide it here. Tokens expire after about an hour; if a later call

tools.name: list_my_programs
tools.description: List your saved Rhylthyme schedules. Requires a login token from the login tool.

tools.name: load_program
tools.description: Load a specific saved program by ID. Returns a markdown summary plus a live-timeline URL.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List the recorded executions of one saved program, newest first: when it ran, how it ended, and the actual makespan against the planned one. A run record is written whenever the live timeline is played (or the terminal runner is used); it is what makes the planned durations checkable against reality

tools.name: load_run
tools.description: Open one recorded execution by run id: planned versus actual start, end and duration for every step, what ended each step (a person, a timer, an abort), time the clock was paused, and the recorded variance factors. Use it to see where a plan drifts from reality. Requires a login token.

tools.name: calibrate_program
tools.description: Propose new durations for one of the user's saved programs from its recorded runs, with the evidence. For every non-fixed step with enough runs a person ended by hand: the median becomes the proposed default, the 10th/90th percentiles the proposed min/max, widened so the author's own range is never

tools.name: list_public_runs
tools.description: List the runs other people have contributed for one exact program version: when each ran, how it ended, actual against planned total, and the variance factors that run was recorded with. Contribution is opt-in per run and contributed records carry no user id and no step notes, so this is anonymous,

tools.name: search_public_recipes
tools.description: Search the public Rhylthyme catalog of cookable recipes, lab protocols, event templates, and workouts. Returns up to 50 matching programs (id, name, description, view URL) — no sign-in required. The catalog is split by environment: pass environment='kitchen' (default), 'laboratory', 'event' or 'gym'

tools.name: load_public_recipe
tools.description: Load a single public recipe / protocol / workout / event template by id. Returns a markdown summary plus a live-timeline URL (no visualize_schedule call needed).

tools.name: save_program
tools.description: Save a Rhylthyme program to your account. If a program with the same programId already exists, it will be updated. Requires a login token.

tools.name: preview_timeline
tools.description: Render a Rhylthyme program as a static Gantt-chart image so the user can SEE what the live timeline looks like, without committing to opening the live URL. Use this when the user asks for a 'preview' or 'picture' of the timeline, or when you have just built a freehand program and want to give the us

tools.name: get_renderer_source
tools.description: Returns the source code of the open-source Rhylthyme timeline renderer (Apache-2.0, ~9KB, zero dependencies). Use this when you're building an HTML artifact and the artifact sandbox blocks external scripts (e.g., Claude.ai's CSP only allows cdnjs.cloudflare.com). The returned text is plain JavaScrip

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "analyze_schedule" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: program, finishAt, startAt, history, program_id, token, predictionContext, useDurations

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_environment" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Create a Rhylthyme environment definition with resource constraints for a workspace (lab, kitchen, bakery, etc.). Returns environment JSON; copy its resourceCon…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_program, visualize_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, login, load_program, search_public_recipes, load_public_recipe, preview_timeline, get_renderer_source · Private data: analyze_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, login, list_my_programs, list_runs, load_run, calibrate_program, list_public_runs, save_program, preview_timeline · Public sink: login · Destructive: validate_program, analyze_schedule, visualize_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, list_runs, load_run, list_public_runs, preview_timeline.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_program, visualize_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, login, load_program, search_public_recipes, load_public_recipe, preview_timeline, get_renderer_source · Private data: analyze_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, login, list_my_programs, list_runs, load_run, calibrate_program, list_public_runs, save_program, preview_timeline · Public sink: login · Destructive: validate_program, analyze_schedule, visualize_schedule, import_from_source, import_text, list_runs, load_run, list_public_runs, preview_timeline

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
